top_choice_rationale: P003 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) honours a settled discovery: the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 time-reversal-invariant topological insulator, predicted in 2005 and first observed in HgTe in 2007, with nearly two decades of independent confirmation. The credit has a defensible core, prediction by Kane and Mele together and first observation by Molenkamp, and a citation limited to that scope avoids both the omission problem with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan and the 2016 topological-phases overlap. P001 is a close second and a result I could fully support, but its correlated-phase mechanism is unsettled and eight years is short; P002 has the cleanest credit but is a measurement achievement whose payoff has not yet arrived; P004 overlaps with the 2012 prize on control of single quantum systems; no award is worse than any of these defensible discoveries.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no credited name on any proposal is a documented connection (Gross, Rubinstein, Van Riet, Uppsala group)
